results.title: Deploy a Private Model Endpoint on Hyperstack
results.author: Fareed Khan
highlights:
Updated on 1 Oct 2026

# Dedicated Inference: Deploy a Private Model Endpoint on Hyperstack

...

### Key Takeaways

- Hyperstack Dedicated Inference puts one open-weight model on GPUs reserved for your organisation, behind a private, API key-protected HTTPS endpoint.
- The Deploy AI wizard sizes the GPU to the model, its context and its concurrency, checks stock, creates the machine and installs vLLM in one pass.
- Sizing is arithmetic: model weights plus KV cache plus runtime overhead, checked against 90 per cent of the card’s advertised VRAM.
- Every endpoint speaks the OpenAI-compatible chat completions API, so existing SDKs and client libraries work unchanged; agentic tool calling works too, described in the prompt rather than the OpenAI tools parameter, since vLLM only turns that parameter on when its server is launched with matching tool-call flags.
- The endpoint provisions on demand and bills per minute at the flavour’s hourly rate, for as long as the machine runs.

...

## Sizing and Cost in Practice

A dedicated endpoint bills per minute at the hourly rate of the flavour it runs on, for as long as the machine is running, regardless of how many requests it serves. The Deploy AI wizard provisions on demand only; Reserved and Spot are not options inside the wizard itself.

Rates follow the standard virtual machine rates in the Pricebook, the same rates that apply to any Hyperstack virtual machine.

What an always-on endpoint costs, on demand

Published on-demand hourly rates multiplied by 730 hours, the same monthly convention the wizard’s own “always-on” estimate uses.

Chart: estimated monthly cost if run continuously on demand, $365 for the NVIDIA RTX A6000 and $730 for the NVIDIA L40.

Hourly rates from the Hyperstack GPU pricing page.

| GPU | VRAM | Memory bandwidth | On demand |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NVIDIA RTX A6000 | 48 GB GDDR6 | 768 GB/s | $0.50/hr |
| NVIDIA L40 | 48 GB GDDR6 | 864 GB/s | $1.00/hr |

Both cards carry the same 48 GB of VRAM, so the choice between them for a model this size is about throughput rather than fit.

results.title: AI Infra Summit 2026 Insights
results.author: Olly Brooks
highlights:
I think this is a healthy shift for the industry, because training is episodic and you can plan for it, budget for it and live with the occasional delay. Inference runs every hour of every day and its cost scales with usage rather than ambition, so once a product takes off, the inference bill becomes the line item that decides whether the unit economics hold together. It is a shift we planned for, and it is the reason Hyperstack Secure Private Cloud gives enterprises dedicated, single-tenant GPU clusters with zero oversubscription. Inference latency is never at the mercy of whoever else is sharing the hardware, because nobody else is. Our Dedicated Cloud tier lets teams consume that capacity as GPU VMs through the same Hyperstack portal and API used for our public cloud regions and serve inferencing endpoints on hardware nobody else touches. A fixed monthly contract gives finance a number they can plan against, which matters a great deal when inference volume is the thing growing fastest.

For teams that are not ready for a 12-month dedicated commitment, the NVIDIA B300 is available on-demand on Hyperstack at $7.40/hr. That is a practical way to benchmark production inference on current-generation hardware before deciding how much capacity to lock in.

highlights:
depl ... Nex

...

## What it costs

 Prices are in US dollars, VAT not stated, read 22 September 2026. One H100 SXM 80 GB with 24 vCPU and 240 GB of RAM costs $3.20 an hour on demand, which is $2,336 a month if you run it for all 730 hours. A reserved rate is advertised "from $2.72 an hour", about 15% less, but the term you have to sign for is not published anywhere, so the commitment behind that discount cannot be worked out in advance. The cheapest GPU is an RTX A4000 at $0.15 an hour, or $110 a month. Hyperstack also publishes spot prices, which most boutique GPU clouds do not: H100 PCIe at $2.00, A100 at $1.08, L40 at $0.80 and RTX A6000 at $0.40 an hour. No eight-GPU node is sold as its own product with its own price. Storage is quoted as roughly $0.10 per TB per hour, which works out at about $0.073 per GB a month, or $73 per TB. Egress and ingress are free. A public IPv4 address costs $0.00672 an hour, about $4.91 a month.

 Billing runs per minute according to the pricing and billing-policy pages, although a second documentation page describes it as hourly. Two things will catch a small buyer out. A stopped virtual machine still bills in full: Hyperstack's own documentation says "billing continues for all resources, as they remain reserved exclusively for that VM". Only hibernation removes the GPU, CPU and RAM charge, and even then the root disk keeps billing at about $0.07 per GB a month and attached volumes keep billing at the standard rate. Running out of credit does not stop the meter either, and the documentation is blunt about it: "Reaching a zero balance does not stop billing. Resources on your account continue to accrue charges, which can take your balance negative until you recharge or the resources are removed." Accounts are prepaid by default and paid by card through Stripe with 3D Secure, and postpaid invoicing needs sales approval. The smallest realistic monthly bill for someone leaving one machine running is an RTX A4000 at $109.50, a public IP at $4.91 and a 100 GB volume at about $7.30, so roughly $122 a month. Swap in an H100 SXM and the same sum comes to about $2,341.

...

Signup is self-serve with a card, and no identity or business verification is documented. No published GPU quota applies to a new account, though the documentation points you at sales for increases or specialised access, so whether a brand-new account can start an eight-GPU H100 job on day one is not something the vendor states. Your balance has to cover everything already running plus one hour of the new machine before it will launch. The real constraint looks like stock rather than paperwork: a one-star review from July 2026 describes GPU inventory as "basically non-existent".

...

Compliance is where the published record thins out. NexGen Cloud's security page still presents SOC 2 Type 1 as a Q2 2025 target with Type 2 to follow, while a support article claims Type 2 has been achieved, and no report date or auditor is published either way. ISO 27001 was promised for early 2026 and there was still no certificate on the site in September 2026. The CLOUD Act is not addressed. Support runs through a Zendesk portal with tickets and live chat plus email, with no published hours or response targets, and prioritised support is sold as a feature of the Premium Postpaid tier, which tells you what the standard tier is not. The service level agreement link in the site footer returned a 404 on 22 September 2026, so there is no uptime figure or service credit schedule to quote. On Trustpilot the score is 2.5 from eight unprompted reviews, split 37% five-star and 63% one-star with nothing in between, and the company has not replied to any of them. The one-star themes are dated and specific: undisclosed storage charges leaving a negative balance of $29.26 (August 2026), no GPU ... (July 2026), support waits of 30 minutes and chat sessions disconnecting instantly (June and July 2026), and broken VM ports after a restart with a refund refused (June 2025). The August 2026 billing complaint matches Hyperstack's own documented policy, which makes it corroborated rather than anecdotal. No outage, breach, regulator action or lawsuit was found on the public record.

...

## Pricing

Minimum commitment: $2,336 ($2,336/mo × 1 seat × 1 month (no commitment)). The least you can spend before walking away; excludes numbers, minutes and add-ons.

results.title: Cheapest GPU Cloud 2026: H100 and A100 Hourly Prices
results.author: Louis Corneloup
highlights:
Hyperstack has the cheapest on-demand H100 and A100 80GB among eight GPU clouds, checked on vendor pricing pages on October 10, 2026.

Louis Corneloup Founder, Dupple · Updated October 28, 2026 · 9 min read

For one GPU running 100 hours a month, Hyperstack is the cheapest on-demand H100 at $2.50 an hour, or $250 for the month. It is also the cheapest A100 80GB at $1.35 an hour, or $135. Both prices are on Hyperstack's own pricing page, read on October 10, 2026. RunPod is next for an H100 at $2.89 an hour, while AWS and Azure charge more than twice Hyperstack's rate per GPU.

The hourly rate is only part of the bill. Some providers rent only eight-GPU nodes, and some bill CPU and memory on top of the GPU. This page puts eight providers with fixed list prices on one basis: the on-demand price per GPU, dated, with the smallest unit you can rent shown next to it. A ninth entry, Lium, is a GPU marketplace, so its figures are the lowest live listings on a later date and sit at the bottom of each table.

...

Every price was verified on vendor pages, Oct 2026, read on each provider's own pricing page or price list on October 10, 2026, in US dollars. The ranking uses on-demand rates only; spot and reserved rates come further down because they carry conditions. "Smallest on-demand unit" means the fewest GPUs a provider lets you rent at its listed rate. When a provider sells only eight-GPU nodes, its per-GPU figure is the node price divided by eight, and the node price sits next to it. The scenario is one H100 80GB and one A100 80GB, each running 100 hours a month, which is the load of a fine-tuning run or a batch inference job.

...

## The on-demand table

Prices are per GPU per hour, cheapest H100 first for the eight fixed-price providers. Modal bills per second, so its hourly figure is the per-second rate times 3,600. Lium's row shows the lowest live marketplace listing on October 28, 2026.

| Lambda | $3.29/hr (PCIe), $4.29/hr (SXM), 1 GPU; $3.99/hr (SXM, 8 GPUs) | $2.79/hr, 8-GPU instance only | 1 GPU for H100, 8 GPUs for A100 80GB | Sales tax extra |
| Modal | $3.95/hr (H100 SXM5) | $2.50/hr | 1 GPU | Per second, CPU and memory extra |
| DigitalOcean | $4.41/hr | No on-demand A100 plan | 1 or 8 GPUs per Droplet | Per hour |

## What 100 GPU-hours costs

Cost is the hourly rate times the hours: $2.50 x 100 = $250. The table below applies that to each provider's smallest unit. Where that unit is eight GPUs, the figure is the whole node.

Spot capacity costs less and can be reclaimed by the provider, so it suits jobs that save checkpoints. Hyperstack's spot H100 PCIe is $2.00 an hour and its spot A100 is $1.08. CoreWeave's spot 8-GPU H100 node is $19.71 an hour, about $2.46 per GPU, and its A100 node is $9.65, about $1.21 per GPU.

Hyperstack also lists reserved rates starting at $1.75 for an H100 and $0.95 for an A100. Reserved rates suit a steady load you can plan months ahead, while spot suits interruptible batch work.

...

Among the eight fixed-price providers, Hyperstack is the cheapest on demand, as read on its pricing page on October 10, 2026. RunPod's H100 PCIe at $2.89 an hour is next, and Lambda's single-GPU PCIe is $3.29. The lowest price on the page is Lium's marketplace, where the lowest live H100 PCIe listing on October 28, 2026 was $1.30 an hour. Hyperstack's spot H100 PCIe is $2.00 an hour, but spot capacity can be reclaimed.

...

Rental rates change without notice, so check the vendor page before you commit a budget. Devshot's newsletter tracks the price moves that developers act on, at devshot.co.

results.title: GPU clouds with per-second billing and no monthly base fee
results.author: Dora Pruteanu
highlights:
Dora Pruteanu 14 October 2026 7 min read Updated 15 October 2026

...

GPU clouds by billing unit: the provider table
2. Base fees and minimum runtime
3. What a stopped instance still costs
4. Per-second billing for short jobs
5. Choosing a provider
6. Frequently asked questions
7. Sources

In short

Lyceum and Exoscale bill GPU compute by the second with no monthly base fee; Hyperstack bills per minute, and Nebius, OVHcloud, Scaleway and Verda list hourly rates. Hetzner's GEX line is dedicated servers with a one-time setup fee. Between jobs, storage and reserved IPs still cost money. Lyceum's and Verda's rates were read on 14 October 2026, the other providers' values on 24 September 2026.

...

- Lyceum's on-demand GPU virtual machines are billed per second with no subscription and no monthly minimum, with 1, 2, 4 or 8 GPUs per instance; the H100 lists at $3.49 per GPU-hour, against $4.50 at Nebius (Lyceum read 14 October 2026).
- Exoscale also bills resources by the second with no up-front costs.
- Hetzner's GPU offering is the GEX line of dedicated servers with monthly and hourly rates plus a one-time setup fee, not per-second cloud VMs.
- A stopped instance still costs money: OVHcloud bills the public IPv4 option at €0.0027 per hour, about €1.97 per month, from October 2026, and Verda lists NVMe storage at $0.20 per GiB-month.
- No monthly base fee appears on any of the eight providers' pricing pages; Nebius states a $25 minimum first payment.

...

A team that wants to pay only for the seconds a GPU runs can use Lyceum's on-demand GPU virtual machines, billed per second with no subscription [1] and launched with 1, 2, 4 or 8 GPUs per instance [2]. Lyceum's billing has no monthly minimum, and prepaid credits do not expire [3]. On its on-demand table, read 14 October 2026, the H100 lists at $3.49 per GPU-hour, the A100 at $1.89 and the L40S at $1.45 [1].

| Provider | On-demand price per GPU-hour | Minimum term | Billing unit | GPUs per instance |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Lyceum | H100 $3.49; A100 $1.89; L40S $1.45 | None | Per second | 1, 2, 4 or 8 |
| Exoscale | – | None; no long-term commitments | Per second | – |
| Hetzner | – | One-time setup fee; monthly term | Monthly or hourly (dedicated server) | 1 |
| Hyperstack | Hourly list per GPU model, billed by the minute | – | Per minute | – |
| Nebius | H100 $4.50; H200 $5.40; L40S from $1.55 [4] | $25 minimum first payment | Per GPU-hour listed | – |
| OVHcloud | A100 $3.07 [5] | – | Per hour | 1, 2 or 4 |
| Scaleway | L4 €0.79; H100 and L40S – [6] | – | Per hour | 1, 2, 4 or 8 |
| Verda | H100 $4.13; H200 $5.38; A100 $1.98 (read 14 October 2026) [7] | – | Per hour | 1, 2, 4 or 8 |

...

The billing unit divides the field into three groups. Lyceum and Exoscale bill by the second [1]; Exoscale's pricing page states that resources are billed by the second, with no up-front costs and no long-term commitments. [8] Hyperstack bills per minute; its pricing FAQ states that the on-demand prepaid platform bills for each minute of use. [9] Hetzner's GEX line consists of dedicated GPU servers with monthly pricing and a one-time setup fee, not per-second virtual machines. [10] Nebius, OVHcloud, Scaleway and Verda publish per-hour rates and make no per-second claim on their pricing pages. [4] [6] [7]

...

No monthly base fee appears on any of the eight pricing pages, and Lyceum states that its billing has no monthly minimum. [3] Two minimums do appear: Hetzner's GEX servers carry a one-time setup fee, and Nebius states a $25 minimum for the first payment. [4] Readers who need a partial node rather than a full eight-GPU server can compare per-GPU rates in the separate guide to partial-node rentals.

...

Two costs survive a stopped GPU, and neither appears in the headline hourly rate.

- Storage: Verda lists NVMe storage at $0.20 per GiB-month. [7] Nebius lists block volumes without data replication from $0.0530 per GiB-month. [4] OVHcloud's billing guide states the Classic Volume costs $0.000066 per GB per hour. [11] Hyperstack lists storage at approximately $0.10 per TB per hour. [9] 
- IP addresses: OVHcloud bills the public IPv4 address at €0.0027 per hour, about €1.97 per month, as a separate line from 1 October 2026. [12] Hyperstack charges $0.00672043 per hour for a public IP address. [9] Nebius lists public IP addresses and egress traffic as free. [4]

...

The billing unit matters most for short jobs. On per-second billing (Lyceum, Exoscale) or per-minute billing (Hyperstack), a ten-minute job is billed as ten minutes. A provider that lists only hourly rates bills at least the started hour, so the same job costs six times the ten-minute figure. The effective premium on short, bursty work therefore grows with the billing unit, which is the same effect that makes cold-start behaviour decisive on such platforms; cold-start comparisons cover that side in detail. For a project that sits idle between runs, storage and reserved IPs, not the GPU rate, can dominate the bill; the drivers of a monthly inference bill are worked through separately.

...

Do these GPU clouds charge a monthly base fee?

No monthly base fee appears on any of the eight pricing pages read on 24 September 2026 (Lyceum's and Verda's on 14 October 2026). The closest things to a fixed charge are Hetzner's one-time setup fee on its GEX dedicated servers and Nebius's $25 minimum first payment, which is a payment threshold rather than a recurring fee.

results.title: GPU pricing is increasing across the board, but the severity of those increases varies greatly across providers.
highlights:
# GPU pricing is increasing across the board, but the severity of those increases varies greatly across providers. · 2026-09-22T00:00:00+00:00

GPU pricing is increasing across the board, but the severity of those increases varies greatly across providers.

Take H100 pricing as an example.

In 2026, providers in our network have raised their H100 rates by an average of 31.6%.

However, between these providers, their individual H100 pricing has increased as much as 47.5%, and as little as 13.6%.

Movement in GPU pricing as a whole only tells part of the story.

There is still significant price variance between operators, even those with near identical architectures.

highlights:
# Nebius hikes AI cloud prices again as demand for computing power soars

 By Thomson Reuters Sep 17, 2026 | 11:16 AM 

Sept 17 (Reuters) – Cloud provider Nebius said on Thursday it will raise pay-as-you-go prices for leasing selected ​Nvidia chips from October 1, ‌marking the company’s second price hike in three months.

Demand for computing capacity to train and run AI models is surging; rival CoreWeave ‌said ​earlier in the ⁠day that it is ⁠signing contracts at higher prices.

Here are some details:

• Rates for selected Nvidia graphics processing units will rise between ​17% and 21%.

• On-demand rates for some central processing units, made ⁠by AMD and Intel, ⁠and memory offerings have also ​been hiked.

• Prices of some CPU-only instances ​will rise by 25% and those ‌of memory offerings by about 41%, the company said.

• The Amsterdam-based neocloud firm said that customers reserving large-scale clusters ⁠for multiple months can receive commitment discounts.

• Nebius’ price increases follow a quarter of rapid ⁠growth ‌in its AI cloud business, ⁠as the company signed four ​customer ‌contracts averaging more than $1 billion ​each.

• Neocloud ⁠firms like Nebius rent out high-powered chips and data center infrastructure needed for AI models.

results.title: Nebius just confirmed the price increase we flagged as unconfirmed last week. Its live now. | Devanshu Rajput
results.author: Devanshu Rajput
highlights:
# Nebius just confirmed the price increase we flagged as unconfirmed last week. Its live now. | Devanshu Rajput · LinkedIn · 2026-10-01T00:00:00+00:00

**Devanshu Rajput**: Growth & Marketing Intern @ ComputeStacker | Content Marketing | SEO | Market Research | Social Media | AI & Technology.

---

Nebius just confirmed the price increase we flagged as unconfirmed last week. Its live now.

H100 pricing on Nebius went from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU-hour, confirmed directly against their own pricing page, a 17% increase. H200 rose 20%, from $4.50 to $5.40. B300 climbed 21%, reaching $9.50. This is Nebius's second rate hike since May, when H100 was still priced at $2.95.

According to GetDeploying's pricing tracker, the median on-demand H100 across 40 providers sat at $3.42/GPU-hour as of September 28, up 15% year over year. The same tracker puts hyperscaler pricing at roughly 58% above specialized GPU clouds for the same chip.

Nobody builds a futures market for a commodity that's reliably getting cheaper. CME Group is launching GPU rental price futures on October 5. That alone signals where this market expects prices to go next.

If a provider quoted you a GPU rate more than a few weeks ago, it's worth checking that number again before you plan a budget around it.
